Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(AB=AC=1\). Put

\[
AP=x,\qquad AQ=y.
\]

The rays are separated by \(20^\circ,46^\circ,26^\circ\), so by the Law of Cosines,

\[
\begin{aligned}
BP^2&=1+x^2-2x\cos20^\circ,\\
PQ^2&=x^2+y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ,\\
QC^2&=1+y^2-2y\cos26^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(BP=PQ=QC\), we get

\[
1-2x\cos20^\circ=y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ \tag{1}
\]

and

\[
x^2-2x\cos20^\circ=y^2-2y\cos26^\circ. \tag{2}
\]

Subtracting gives

\[
2y(x\cos46^\circ-\cos26^\circ)=x^2-1,
\]

so

\[
y=\frac{1-x^2}{2(\cos26^\circ-x\cos46^\circ)}. \tag{3}
\]

Solving the resulting one-variable equation (with \(0<x<1\), as \(P,Q\) are inside the triangle) gives the interior solution

\[
x=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Then from (3),

\[
y=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Now work in triangle \(APC\). We have

\[
\angle PAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ.
\]

Let \(\theta=\angle APC\). By the Law of Cosines,

\[
PC^2=x^2+1-2x\cos72^\circ.
\]

Using \(x=\dfrac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}\), one obtains

\[
PC=\frac{\sin72^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Then

\[
\cos\theta
=\frac{x-\cos72^\circ}{PC}
=\frac{\sin34^\circ-\cos72^\circ\sin74^\circ}{\sin72^\circ}.
\]

Using product-to-sum,

\[
\sin34^\circ-\cos72^\circ\sin74^\circ
=\cos74^\circ\sin72^\circ,
\]

so

\[
\cos\theta=\cos74^\circ.
\]

Thus

\[
\theta=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
